## D8 at a glance

- **The model gates:** held-out AUC {{< var li.auc >}} against a gate of
  {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}} (interval {{< var li.boot.auc.lo >}}–{{< var li.boot.auc.hi >}}),
  and top-quintile lift {{< var li.lift >}}× against {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}×, on the
  held-out {{< var li.test_share >}} of the booked book. Both met; the model gets
  {{< var ceiling.li.share_of_reach >}} of the way to the data's ceiling and beats every single
  input with a paired interval above zero ([8.5](performance.qmd)).
- **An offer is `eligible`:** {{< var li.n_offered >}} accounts, {{< var li.offer_share >}} of
  the book — not the {{< var li.n_amount_positive >}} with a positive recommended amount
  ([8.1](purpose.qmd#li-funnel)).
- **The cohort gates cannot fail:** {{< var li.cohort_gate.n_cannot_fail >}} of the
  {{< var li.gate.n_gates >}} training gates — the aggregate ROE by construction, the PD and
  utilisation comparisons on this book — so no gate tests whether the offers are good
  (finding 1, [8.7](limitations.qmd)).
- **Quote the held-out offers:** {{< var li.offers.n_train >}} of the offers are the model's
  training rows; the held-out offers' label rate is {{< var li.offers_ho.observed >}}
  against a predicted {{< var li.offers_ho.predicted >}}, within tolerance (finding 2).
- **Offers and Early Warning:** by tier the offers are flagged less than the book; by trigger
  more, mostly through the utilisation rules they are selected on; their deterioration rate,
  {{< var li.offers.det.rate >}} against {{< var li.book.det.rate >}}, is not distinguishable
  from the book's ([8.5](performance.qmd#li-ews)).
- **Six open findings** the chapter raises about its own model, rules and gate
  ([8.7](limitations.qmd)).
:::

Line Increase looks over the booked book and decides which accounts to offer more credit
before they ask ([8.1](purpose.qmd)). It is a gradient-boosted model (LightGBM) on
{{< var li.n_features >}} features of each account's on-book state, its origination file and
the Business Credit Score's PD ([8.2](data.qmd)), followed by three rules: a ceiling on the
scorecard's PD, amount rules that cap the increase three ways, and an incremental-ROE test
that prices the increase with the pricing engine ([8.3](methodology.qmd)). It proposes offers
for a credit officer to review and changes no limit by itself, which makes it Tier 2
([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#risk-tiering)).

{{< include ../../_generated/li-headline.md >}}

The model figures are measured on the held-out {{< var li.test_share >}} of the
{{< var li.n_book >}} booked accounts: {{< var li.n_test >}} accounts the model never saw while
it was fitted, redrawn exactly as `line_increase/src/train.py` drew them
([8.2](data.qmd#li-split)). Every number in the chapter is a named fact, recomputed through the
module's own functions — the saved model on `compute_line_increase_features`,
`recommended_amount`, `incremental_roe`, `candidates` and `segments` — by `python verify.py`;
the [fact index](../../reference/facts.qmd) gives each one's source and population. The
chapter documents the model, rules and gate as committed: it changes none of them.
